sources.title: Ghana’s first biennial transparency report to the UNFCCC under Article 13 of the Paris Agreement
sources.organization: Environmental Protection Agency, Ghana; Ministry of Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation
sources.temporal_coverage: National climate impacts, adaptation progress and institutional gaps reported through 2024
sources.methodology: EPA’s first UNFCCC BTR used an 18-month interagency reporting process with technical and stakeholder review.
sources.limitations: The local vulnerability ranking summarizes a cited 2024 assessment; the BTR also reports local data, funding and capacity gaps.

sources.title: Climate Change Vulnerability Assessment for the Kintampo Municipal Assembly
sources.organization: Government of Ghana, Environmental Protection Agency; authored by Yaw Agyeman Boafo for Foresight Planners and Research Africa Limited
sources.temporal_coverage: Household and qualitative assessment in 2022; historical climate review 1980–2020; projections through 2100
sources.methodology: Mixed qualitative and quantitative municipal assessment, including a 153-household survey in nine purposively selected communities, interviews and participatory mapping.
sources.limitations: Community rankings are based on a purposive, small-area sample and the report’s composite indices; they are not municipality-wide probability estimates.

sources.title: Farmer-herder conflicts in northern Ghana amid climate change: causes and policy responses
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate and conflict mechanisms and local responses reported through 2022
sources.methodology: Case-based policy brief draws on police and chiefs’ records, interviews, cited research and northern climate trends; it is not a national causal estimate.
sources.limitations: The author identifies political, tenure and identity drivers alongside climate and warns local cases may be under-reported.

sources.title: Ghana Disaster Management and Risk Finance Strategy Framework and Implementation Plan (2025–2030)
sources.organization: Government of Ghana, National Disaster Management Organisation, with technical support from UNDP’s Insurance and Risk Finance Facility
sources.temporal_coverage: Regional disaster risk and coping-capacity baseline based on 2021 assessment; framework and implementation plan for 2025–2030
sources.methodology: Regional profile builds on the 2021 PDC-NADMO Risk and Vulnerability Assessment and Disaster Management Analysis.
sources.limitations: Indices are region-level summaries, not district estimates; an approved strategy does not establish implementation or outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF p. 118, printed p. 119, section 4.2.1 and Figure 13
claims.paraphrase: The BTR reports vulnerability rising from coastal zones through the transition belt to northern savannas; Upper West is highest, while Greater Accra, Ashanti and Central are lowest across 216 districts and six ecological zones.
claims.limitations: The BTR summarizes an external 2024 assessment; its figure does not provide district-specific scores in the inspected passage.

claims.paraphrase: The BTR reports local-government shortages of finance and staff, weak rural/remote data integration, limited technical capacity and coordination, and early-warning and monitoring gaps that restrict preparedness.
geographies: Rural and remote communities in Ghana
claims.limitations: These are national-report findings about local systems, not a quantified comparison of named districts.

claims.paraphrase: The BTR reports warning communications at NADMO headquarters and 20 subnational offices, plus community disaster-risk committees trained in local assessment, response planning and preparedness.
claims.limitations: The BTR describes arrangements and training, not independently evaluated warning reach or effectiveness.

claims.locator: PDF p. 75, printed p. 66, section 3.3.2.5 and Figure 3.23
claims.paraphrase: The assessment ranks Busuama, Dawadawa and Alhassan Akura as Kintampo’s most vulnerable communities and Kintampo least; Busuama combines low capacity, rainfed livelihoods, weak service/market access and flood-prone homes.
claims.limitations: Ranking uses 153 households from nine purposively selected communities, not a probability-representative municipal sample.

claims.paraphrase: Kintampo and Cheranda scored high in adaptive capacity, linked to credit, remittances, markets, irrigation, crop diversity and extension; Busuama, Dawadawa, Alhassan Akura and New Longoro scored very low.
claims.limitations: Community-level indices are based on the assessment’s 2022 household survey and selected indicators.

claims.paraphrase: The assessment identifies Cheranda, Babato, Dawadawa and New Longoro among Kintampo communities most affected by bushfires, which damage vegetation and crops including cashew.
institutions: Ministry of Food and Agriculture municipal office
claims.limitations: The assessment says local data on human-caused fires are lacking and notes climatic and land-management factors.

claims.locator: PDF p. 6, section ‘Climate change and resource scarcity as exacerbating factors’
claims.paraphrase: In Gushegu, the author links heat stress and resource scarcity to herders’ mobility and feeding adaptations that damage crops or breach tree tenure and can trigger farmer-herder disputes.
claims.limitations: The brief treats climate as an exacerbating factor alongside political, tenure and identity drivers; it does not estimate an independent effect.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The author says climate-driven heat and scarcity alter herder strategies that can damage crops and provoke conflict (PDF p. 6).

claims.locator: PDF p. 7, section ‘Approaches to farmer-herder conflicts and their limits’
claims.paraphrase: A Gushegu chief-led committee hears farmer-herder disputes and may decide compensation, but is informal and cannot enforce decisions; some parties distrust its decisions or allege favoritism.
claims.limitations: The finding is localized and based on interviews; it is not a formal evaluation of all local dispute mechanisms.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 15–16, Table 1, Regional Risk Profile
claims.paraphrase: The strategy assigns coastal flood/sea-level-rise risk to Greater Accra, Volta and Central; river flooding to Northern, Upper East and Eastern; drought and heat to Northern, Upper East, Upper West and Savannah.
claims.limitations: The table is a regional profile, not a district-level risk assessment.

claims.locator: PDF p. 17, Table 2, Coping Capacity by Region
claims.paraphrase: The strategy’s coping-capacity index rates Savannah, North East, Oti and Northern very low (0.184–0.255), versus Greater Accra very high (0.952).
claims.limitations: The index is the strategy’s regional composite, not a direct measure of individual or conflict-affected household capacity.

claims.locator: PDF p. 15, section 2.1.3, Gender and Vulnerability Dimension
claims.paraphrase: The strategy identifies women and girls, people with disabilities and older people in rural and low-income areas as facing higher disaster risk amid limited resources, decision power and protective services.
geographies: Rural and low-income areas in Ghana
claims.limitations: The strategy summarizes existing evidence and does not disaggregate these risks by region.

Publisher PDF request returned an access/server error; it was not used. The same report was accessed from CDA’s public PDF URL.

search_audit.query: Ghana district climate vulnerability NADMO local committees report PDF
search_audit.outcome: Located the full BTR, regional risk strategy and Government of Ghana Kintampo municipal vulnerability assessment; the latter provides named community rankings and field-survey evidence.

search_audit.query: Ghana climate change farmer herder conflict adaptation resources Gushegu district primary report PDF
search_audit.outcome: Opened Ahmed’s case-based policy brief; it explicitly describes heat/resource scarcity, herder adaptations and farmer-herder conflict in Gushegu, while naming political, tenure and identity drivers.

search_audit.query: Ghana violent conflict insecurity disrupt climate adaptation disaster response local government climate finance report
search_audit.outcome: No inspected source documented armed conflict disrupting climate-adaptation delivery. The Gushegu brief examines dispute mechanisms and the BTR describes local early-warning and capacity constraints; no reverse causal claim is coded.

search_audit.query: Ghana disaster risk coping capacity regional Savannah North East Oti NADMO resilience strategy PDF
search_audit.outcome: The full NADMO-UNDP strategy reports a region-level coping-capacity index; the BTR reports subnational warning systems and community disaster-risk committees. The Kintampo assessment gives named-community adaptive-capacity comparisons.

gaps: The official Ghana National Adaptation Plan linked from the UNFCCC record could not be inspected because its 18.1 MB PDF exceeded browser retrieval limits; no claims use its metadata or indexed text.
The inspected reverse-FCV search did not locate evidence that armed conflict disrupted climate-adaptation delivery; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
Kintampo community rankings derive from 153 households in nine purposively selected communities and should not be generalized to the municipality or Ghana.
The source-reported farmer-herder mechanism in Gushegu is conditional and multi-causal; no independent national climate-conflict estimate was found.
